confidentUnsupported.evidence: "This suggests an issue with the drain hose installation. If it sits too low or deep in the waste, water can siphon out" — after customer stated nothing is leaking or siphoning and water only flows during the drying programme.

blockingLoop.evidence: Customer asked 'Is that normal for a washer-dryer, yes or no?' three times; assistant repeated unplug/turn-off preamble in three turns, pushed the drain hose check twice, and asked noise-type questions twice after the customer had already described the sound.

rationale: The hidden truth is a perfectly normal water-cooled condenser drying cycle, which the customer effectively handed to the assistant ('the manual says water is used during drying for condensation', clothes dry, no leaks, no codes). The assistant ignored all of this, opened with an unjustified stop-use and isolation warning, fixated on a drain-hose siphon fault that nothing supported, and then drifted into generic washing-machine noise triage (grinding/squeal, turn the drum by hand) unrelated to a trickle of water during drying. It never answered the direct yes/no question and looped on safety preambles and already-answered questions, leaving the homeowner worse off than before they asked.
